mainTopic: Which children of עמוני and מצרי converts may marry into כהונה or the קהל, and the dispute of רבי שמעון and the חכמים over מצרי and אדומי women
overview: רבי זכאי teaches that the פסוק about the כהן גדול's wife includes a גיורת מכנה, a girl born after her parents converted, as fit for כהונה. רבי יוחנן says the words עמיו and מעמיו include more: a girl 'from two peoples,' meaning the daughter of an עמוני and a בת ישראל. In a second version, the גמרא asks how we know the daughter of a second-generation מצרי is fit. It proves this from what the עמוני case and the מצרי-and-מצרית case have in common. רב יוסף then understands a teaching of רב יהודה in this light. Next comes a ברייתא that calls the daughter of an עמוני and a בת ישראל unfit for כהונה, and רבי יוחנן rejects it. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's dispute about מצרי and אדומי women. It tries to explain the חכמים' refutation of רבי שמעון from עריות and ממזר, rejects that, and lands on חלל, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. רבי שמעון answers that he does not follow that view and is stating a received הלכה, supported by the word 'sons.' רבי יהודה reads the same פסוק as depending on birth, and רבי יוחנן begins to explain why רבי יהודה needed that reading, an explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי זכאי's teaching: a girl born to converts may marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי זכאי quotes a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. The פסוק 'a virgin of his own people' includes a גיורת מכנה, and she is fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי זכאי taught in front of רבי יוחנן: 'But a virgin of his own people shall he take as a wife.' This comes to include a girl who was a convert from birth, showing she may marry into כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that רבי זכאי taught. It says that a girl born to parents who had already converted may marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about the כהן גדול marrying a בתולה 'from his people.' רבי זכאי reads it as including a גיורת מכנה. Her parents converted before she was conceived, so she was Jewish from her very start.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who was a convert from the start: conceived and born after her parents converted
Fit to marry a כהן
A virgin from his own people (from the פסוק about the כהן גדול)
To include (this case in the rule)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Zakkai taught
before Rabbi Yochanan:
"But a virgin of his own people shall he take as a wife"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14

phrases.english: this comes to include a girl who was a convert from her very beginning,
that she is fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי זַכַּאי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with a ברייתא that supports the earlier discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גיורת מכנה is fit for כהונה, learned from 'בתולה מעמיו.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the verse includes even more
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he learns from 'עמיו / מעמיו' that the פסוק includes a girl 'from two peoples.' He challenges רבי זכאי for including only a גיורת מכנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: I learn from 'his people' and 'of his people' that the פסוק includes a virgin who comes from two peoples. And you say only a girl born to converts, and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on רבי זכאי. He says the פסוק includes a wider group than just a girl born to converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads extra meaning from the added מ in 'מעמיו.' He uses it to include a girl whose parents come from two different peoples. His question 'and nothing more?' is a challenge: your reading is too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: I teach / I learn (this is how I read it)
Two peoples (parents from two different groups)
And nothing more?

phrases.english: And he said to him:
I teach "his people," "of his people"
phrases.notes: He reads the extra letter מ in מעמיו as widening who is included.

phrases.english: to include a virgin who comes from two peoples,
and you say a girl who was a convert from birth
and no more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זכאי's reading as too narrow and widens it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זכאי's limit of the פסוק to a גיורת מכנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double wording 'עמיו / מעמיו' includes more cases, so stopping at גיורת מכנה is too limited.

steps.title: What does 'two peoples' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי יוחנן meant by 'two peoples.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'two peoples'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what 'two peoples' means. This sets up the next steps, which test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two peoples' is not clear on its own. The גמרא needs to find a case that adds something beyond רבי זכאי's גיורת מכנה. Otherwise רבי יוחנן's challenge would make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request to define)

phrases.english: What is "two peoples"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the key phrase in רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case of 'two peoples' רבי יוחנן means

steps.title: Not an Ammonite man married to an Ammonite woman
steps.stepSummary: Suppose it meant an עמוני married to an עמונית, called 'two peoples' because the men are forbidden and the women permitted. Then it would be the same as a גיורת מכנה, so this cannot be the meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say it means an עמוני man who married an עמונית woman. 'Two peoples' would mean that their males are forbidden and their females permitted. But that is just the same as a girl born to converts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one answer and rejects it. If 'two peoples' meant an Ammonite couple, רבי יוחנן would add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עמוני man may never marry into the Jewish people, but an עמונית woman may. So the nation is like 'two peoples.' Still, the daughter of two Ammonite converts is simply a girl born to converts. רבי זכאי already included her, so רבי יוחנן's 'and nothing more?' would not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)
A man from the nation of עמון
Males are forbidden to marry into the Jewish people, but females are permitted
That is the same thing as

phrases.english: If you say an Ammonite man who married an Ammonite woman,
and what does "from two peoples" mean?
that the males are forbidden and the females are permitted,
that is the same as a girl who was a convert from birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'two peoples' as an Ammonite couple
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would be the same as גיורת מכנה, so רבי יוחנן would add nothing.

steps.title: It means an Ammonite man married to a Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: 'Two peoples' means a girl whose father is an עמוני and whose mother is a בת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means an עמוני who married a Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning. The girl's parents truly come from two different peoples, an Ammonite father and a Jewish mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case adds something new. An עמוני man is forbidden to marry a Jewish woman, and still רבי יוחנן says their daughter may marry a כהן. That goes beyond a simple girl born to converts.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the accepted answer)
A Jewish woman by birth

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבי יוחנן's 'two peoples' means a daughter of an עמוני father and a Jewish mother, and she is fit for כהונה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is about an Ammonite man
who married a Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after the first suggestion was rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Two peoples' means a daughter of an עמוני father and a Jewish mother.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יוחנן's words
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי יוחנן adds that the girl comes 'from a people that has two peoples within it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי יוחנן said to him: I learn from 'his people' and 'of his people' that the פסוק includes a virgin who comes from two peoples, and from a people that has two peoples within it. And you say only a girl born to converts, and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of what רבי יוחנן said. It adds one extra phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added words, 'a people that has two peoples within it,' point to nations like עמון, where the men are forbidden and the women permitted. So in this version, the case is a Jewish mother with a father from such a nation. That makes the source narrower than in the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)
A people that has two peoples within it (men and women with different rules)

phrases.english: And some say: he said to him:
I teach "his people," "of his people"
to include a virgin who comes from two peoples,
and from a people that has two peoples within it,
phrases.notes: He means a nation like עמון, whose men and women follow different rules.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ גִּיּוֹרֶת מִכַּנָּהּ וְתוּ לָא?
phrases.english: and you say a girl who was a convert from birth, and no more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רבי יוחנן's challenge from step 2, with an added phrase
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק includes a daughter of a Jewish mother and a father from a nation whose males are forbidden but whose females are permitted.

steps.title: Then where do we learn about the Egyptian's daughter?
steps.stepSummary: Under the second version, the source covers only nations like עמון. So how does רבי יוחנן know that the daughter of a second-generation מצרי is fit for כהונה?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to this version, how does he know that the daughter of a second-generation מצרי is fit for כהונה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version. It no longer seems to have a source for the case of a מצרי's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 'two peoples' was broad enough to cover a מצרי father too. In the second version, the source is limited to 'a people with two peoples in it,' meaning nations like עמון. A מצרי is not like that, so the second version seems to leave this case without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: According to this version
A second-generation Egyptian convert
From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And according to this version,
the daughter of a second-generation Egyptian,
that she is fit for the priesthood — from where does he know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second version for being too narrow
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second version limits the source to nations like עמון, so the daughter of a second-generation מצרי has no source.

steps.title: We cannot learn the Egyptian case from the Ammonite case
steps.stepSummary: Someone might suggest learning the מצרי case from the עמוני case. The גמרא rejects this because עמוני women are fully permitted, which may explain why the daughter is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he learns it from an עמוני who married a Jewish woman: what about the עמוני case? There, the women are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer to its own question and knocks it down right away. The עמוני case has a special feature that the מצרי case does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter of an עמוני may be allowed because עמוני women are permitted to marry into the Jewish people. A מצרי woman is forbidden just like a מצרי man until the third generation. Since that reason does not carry over, we cannot copy the rule from the עמוני case alone. Steps 9–12 find another way to prove it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (a suggested answer)
He learns it (from another case)
What about X? Since X has a special feature (a way to block a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the מצרי's daughter is forbidden. It is only saying that the עמוני case cannot be the source for allowing her.

phrases.english: And if you say that he learns it
from an Ammonite who married a Jewish woman:
what about an Ammonite who married a Jewish woman?
There, the females are permitted.
phrases.notes: Egyptian women are forbidden just like Egyptian men, so this reason does not apply to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּיָלֵיף מֵעַמּוֹנִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a possible answer to step 7 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning the מצרי case from the עמוני case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עמוני women are permitted while מצרי women are not, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: The Egyptian-married-Egyptian case as a counterexample
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 8 with a case where the women of the nation are forbidden, yet the daughter is still permitted: a second-generation מצרי who married a second-generation מצרית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let a second-generation Egyptian man who married a second-generation Egyptian woman prove the point!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering the objection from step 8. That objection said the עמוני case only works because עמוני women are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among the מצרים, women are forbidden just like men. Still, when a second-generation מצרי marries a second-generation מצרית, their daughter is third-generation and permitted. So having forbidden women does not stop the daughter from being permitted, and the point raised in step 8 is not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: A second-generation Egyptian convert, who is still forbidden to marry into the Jewish people
A second-generation Egyptian woman convert, who is also forbidden
"Let it prove": a case brought to show that a suggested difference does not matter

phrases.english: A second-generation Egyptian man who married
phrases.notes: Their child would be third-generation, and the תורה lets the third generation of Egyptians enter the קהל.

phrases.english: a second-generation Egyptian woman will prove it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְרִי שֵׁנִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא מִצְרִית שְׁנִיָּה יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 8 by bringing a case where the women are forbidden and the daughter is still permitted.
steps.raayaObject: That forbidden women in the nation do not stop the daughter from being permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of a second-generation מצרי married to a second-generation מצרית, whose daughter is permitted.

steps.title: That marriage was not a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the מצרי who married a מצרית did nothing wrong, while the case we are asking about is a forbidden marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare to a second-generation Egyptian man who married a second-generation Egyptian woman? His relationship involves no sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second-generation מצרי may marry a second-generation מצרית, so their union is permitted. In our case, though, a second-generation מצרי married a בת ישראל, which is forbidden. Maybe a daughter born from a forbidden union is not fit for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: "What comparison is there to...": the standard opening for pointing out a difference between two cases
"Since": introduces the special feature of the case being compared
A relationship that is itself a sin

phrases.english: What comparison is there to a second-generation Egyptian man
who married a second-generation Egyptian woman,
since his relationship with her is not a sin.
phrases.notes: Our real case is different: a second-generation מצרי who married a Jewish-born woman, which is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִצְרִי שֵׁנִי שֶׁנָּשָׂא מִצְרִית שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁכֵּן אֵין בִּיאָתוֹ בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counterexample from step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning only from the מצרי-married-מצרית case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That marriage was permitted, while our case is a forbidden marriage.

steps.title: Back to the Ammonite case: a sinful marriage, yet the daughter is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that objection with the עמוני who married a בת ישראל: that marriage is a sin, and still the daughter is fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let an Ammonite man who married a Jewish woman prove the point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the עמוני case to answer the objection from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עמוני may not marry a בת ישראל, so that union is a sin. Even so, step 5 taught that their daughter may marry a כהן. So a sinful union does not stop the daughter from being permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An Ammonite convert. The men are forbidden to marry into the Jewish people forever, but the women are permitted
A woman born Jewish

phrases.english: An Ammonite man who married a Jewish woman will prove it.
phrases.notes: This is the girl from step 5, whom רבי יוחנן allows to marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 10 by going back to the עמוני case from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That a forbidden union does not stop the daughter from being permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The daughter of an עמוני and a בת ישראל, who is fit for כהונה.

steps.title: The argument goes in a circle, so learn from what both cases share
steps.stepSummary: Each case has a weak point that the other one covers. Both share one result, a permitted daughter, so the daughter of a second-generation מצרי and a בת ישראל is also permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the argument has come back around to where it started, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof using a צד השוה, a learning from the feature two cases have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עמוני case can be pushed away because its women are permitted. The מצרי-and-מצרית case can be pushed away because the marriage was not a sin. But each case answers the other's weak point, and in both the daughter is permitted. So רבי יוחנן's ruling also covers the daughter of a second-generation מצרי who married a בת ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: "The argument has come back around": the signal that two cases cover each other's weak points
The shared feature of two cases, used to prove a third case

steps.whatToRemember: Neither case alone proves the מצרי ruling, but together they do. The daughter is permitted whether or not the nation's women are forbidden, and whether or not the marriage was a sin.
steps.confusionAlert: The word וכו׳ ("and so on") is not skipping new information. It is shorthand for the standard ending: the two cases are not the same, but what they share teaches the new case.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around, and so on.
phrases.notes: The "and so on" stands for the usual ending: what both cases share proves the מצרי case too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two counterexamples from steps 9 and 11 into one shared-feature proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Based on what the עמוני case and the מצרי case share, the daughter of a second-generation מצרי and a בת ישראל is fit for כהונה.

steps.title: רב יוסף finally understands רב יהודה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that this is what רב יהודה meant when he taught from the words עמיו and מעמיו, which רב יוסף had not understood at the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what I heard רב יהודה say about the words 'his people' and 'from his people', and I did not know what he meant.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף links רבי יוחנן's teaching about 'two peoples' to a lesson he once heard from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה expounded the words עמיו and מעמיו in the פסוק about whom a כהן may marry. Until now רב יוסף did not know what point he was making. Now he sees that it is the same idea as רבי יוחנן's teaching: a girl from 'two peoples', like the daughter of an עמוני and a בת ישראל, may marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: "His people"
"From his people": the extra 'from' (מ) means even from part of his people, hinting at a girl of two peoples
"This is what...": links a new teaching to something already said
"I did not know"

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוחנן's 'two peoples' reading was also taught by רב יהודה, so this way of reading the פסוק has wider support.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This is what I heard Rav Yehuda
say: 'his people', 'from his people',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14. This is the same 'two peoples' reading of the פסוק that רבי יוחנן gave.

phrases.english: and I did not know what he was saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הַיְינוּ דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's 'two peoples' reading and connects it to רב יהודה's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's teaching on עמיו and מעמיו means what רבי יוחנן taught: a girl from two peoples, such as the daughter of an עמוני and a בת ישראל, is fit for כהונה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about an Ammonite woman, her son and her daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports a ברייתא. An Ammonite woman is fit, and her son from an Ammonite man is unfit. Her daughter from an Ammonite man is fit, but only when both parents converted. Otherwise the daughter is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר יהודה came, he said: this is how the reciter taught it: an Ammonite woman is fit, her son from an Ammonite man is unfit, and her daughter from an Ammonite man is fit. When is this said? When both the Ammonite man and the Ammonite woman converted. But her daughter from an Ammonite man is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is brought: a ברייתא listing the status of an Ammonite woman, her son and her daughter. The rest of this section will test each line of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has four parts: the mother is fit, the son is unfit, and the daughter is fit, with a limit at the end. The limit says the daughter is fit only when both parents converted. Otherwise 'her daughter from an Ammonite' is unfit, and the גמרא will soon ask what that last line means.

keyTerms.meaning: An Ammonite woman
Fit, allowed to marry in
Unfit, barred
When is this said? (introduces a limit on the rule)
Who converted

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda came, he said:
This is how the reciter taught before him:
phrases.notes: From the wider discussion, this is רבי זכאי reciting before רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: An Ammonite woman is fit,
her son from an Ammonite man is unfit,
and her daughter from an Ammonite man is fit.
When is this said?
With an Ammonite man and an Ammonite woman who converted,
but her daughter from an Ammonite man is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר: הָכִי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on the same question: the daughter of an Ammonite convert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ammonite woman fit; her son unfit; her daughter fit only when both parents converted, otherwise unfit.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא and calls the first lines obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the reciter to 'go teach it outside.' He then shows that the first two lines teach nothing new. A woman is fit because the פסוק says 'Ammonite man.' A son is unfit because he is an Ammonite.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: go out and teach it outside. What you said, that an Ammonite woman is fit, is simply the rule 'Ammonite man, not Ammonite woman.' Her son from an Ammonite is unfit because he is an Ammonite.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא and begins going through it line by line. He shows that the first two lines are things everyone already knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Go teach it outside' means this ברייתא should not be taught in the בית מדרש. The real problem has not come yet; first he clears away the easy lines. The mother being fit and the son being unfit add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and teach it outside (this teaching is not reliable)
Ammonite man, not Ammonite woman: only men are barred

phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and teach it outside.
phrases.notes: He means: this ברייתא isn't reliable, so don't teach it in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: What you said, that an Ammonite woman is fit,
is just 'an Ammonite man' and not an Ammonite woman.
phrases.notes: The well-known reading of דברים 23:4.

phrases.english: Her son from an Ammonite man is unfit,
because he is an Ammonite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ברייתא from step 14 and starts checking its lines.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ברייתא, starting with its first two lines.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first two lines teach nothing new, and the reason the whole teaching fails comes later.

steps.title: Fit for what? Not for marrying into the nation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'her daughter is fit' could mean. It cannot mean fit to marry into the nation. If even the mother is fit for that, the daughter surely is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And her daughter from an Ammonite is fit: for what? If you say to enter the congregation, now that her mother is fit, do we even need to say it about her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the third line, 'her daughter is fit,' is about. It rules out one obvious meaning, which sets up the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother herself may marry a Jew. So saying the daughter may marry a Jew would be pointless. The line must be teaching something bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: For what?
To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a Jew
Now that (if even this is so)
Is it needed to say?

phrases.english: And her daughter from an Ammonite is fit: for what?
If you say fit to enter the congregation,
now that even her mother is fit,
do we even need to say it about her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third line of the ברייתא.

steps.title: Fit to marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The line must mean the daughter is fit to marry into כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means fit for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16: the daughter is fit to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the only meaning that makes the line teach something new. It also connects to the question from the earlier steps: whether such a daughter may marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: For the priesthood, meaning fit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Rather, fit for the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The daughter is fit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: Which daughter does the last line call unfit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the limit again and asks what 'her daughter from an Ammonite' means. It cannot mean a child of two Ammonites. That girl would just be an ordinary convert, and her law is already known.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? With an Ammonite man and woman who converted, but her daughter from an Ammonite is unfit. What is 'her daughter from an Ammonite'? If you say an Ammonite who married an Ammonite woman, that is just a regular convert!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the closing line of the ברייתא again and asks which daughter it calls unfit. It rules out one meaning, which sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the parents were an Ammonite man and an Ammonite woman who converted, the daughter is a גיורת מכנה. Step 1 already taught that she is fit for כהונה, so she cannot be the daughter this line calls unfit. The line must be about some other case.

keyTerms.meaning: Who married
That is the same as

phrases.english: When is this said?
With an Ammonite man and an Ammonite woman who converted,
but her daughter from an Ammonite man is unfit.
What is 'her daughter from an Ammonite man'?
If you say an Ammonite man who married an Ammonite woman,
that is the same as a girl who was a convert from birth!
phrases.notes: This is the girl from step 1, already taught to be fit for כהונה, so she can't be the one this line calls unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the closing limit of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which daughter the closing line calls unfit.

steps.title: The ברייתא disqualifies the daughter of an Ammonite and a בת ישראל, so it is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The line must mean an Ammonite man who married a בת ישראל. The ברייתא calls their daughter unfit for כהונה. That goes against the accepted ruling, so רבי יוחנן says: go teach it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means an Ammonite man who married a Jewish woman. He said to him: go out and teach it outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the only case left: an Ammonite man and a בת ישראל. This explains why רבי יוחנן threw the ברייתא out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the daughter of an Ammonite man and a בת ישראל is unfit for כהונה. רבי יוחנן's own reading of 'two peoples' (step 5) makes this daughter fit. Since the ברייתא disagrees, רבי יוחנן says it should not be taught.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish woman by birth

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא because it calls the daughter of an Ammonite man and a בת ישראל unfit for כהונה. The accepted view is that she is fit.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Go teach it outside' appears twice. The first time it is just the rejection; only here at the end do we learn the reason.

phrases.english: Rather, it means an Ammonite man who married a Jewish woman,
so he said to him: Go out and teach it outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes step 18 and gives the reason for the rejection in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא disqualifies the daughter of an Ammonite man and a בת ישראל, against the accepted ruling, so רבי יוחנן rejects it.

steps.title: What was the refutation of רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about מצרי and אדומי and asks what the חכמים' 'refutation' of רבי שמעון actually was.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Egyptian and Edomite converts are prohibited only for three generations, etc.' What is the refutation the חכמים mentioned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and asks a question. It is setting up the next step, where we will hear the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון made a קל וחומר to permit מצרי and אדומי women right away. The חכמים told him there is a תשובה, a refutation, but the משנה never says what it is. The גמרא now wants to know what that refutation was.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian convert, banned from marrying into the nation for three generations
An Edomite convert, with the same three-generation ban
A refutation, an answer that knocks down an argument
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

phrases.english: Egyptian and Edomite converts are not prohibited, etc.
What is the refutation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עמוני discussion and opens a new topic in the משנה: the מצרי and אדומי dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly the refutation of רבי שמעון's קל וחומר was.

steps.title: Forbidden relations prove otherwise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the refutation comes from עריות: they reach only three generations, yet they forbid females as well as males.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the refutation is that one can say עריות will prove it. The תורה forbids relatives there only up to three generations, and it forbids the female line and the male line alike.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. He points to עריות as a case that breaks רבי שמעון's logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון reasoned that a ban limited to three generations is weaker, so its women should be permitted. רבי יוחנן shows a case with that same three-generation limit where the women are still forbidden just like the men. So a three-generation limit does not mean women are let off.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relations, mostly close relatives
Will prove, show that an argument fails
Three generations
Males and females

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because one can say:
Let forbidden relations prove it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא אָסַר בָּהֶן אֶלָּא עַד שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת,
phrases.english: for the Torah prohibited them only up to three generations,
both males and females alike!
phrases.notes: His son's daughter and his daughter's daughter are both forbidden. It makes no difference whether the line goes through a son or a daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The refutation is from עריות: a ban limited to three generations that still treats males and females the same.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A three-generation limit does not mean the women are permitted, as עריות show.

steps.title: Forbidden relations are stricter because of כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from עריות, since they carry the strict punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare to עריות? They are punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. It says עריות are too strict to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe עריות forbid women too only because they are so severe, carrying כרת. The ban on מצרי and אדומי has no כרת, so the comparison may not work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How can you compare to...?' A formula for rejecting a comparison
Since, because it has this feature
A severe heavenly punishment, being cut off

phrases.english: How can you compare to forbidden relations,
since they carry כרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עריות have a special strictness (כרת) that might be why their women are also forbidden.

steps.title: Let ממזר prove it instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof: ממזר, which has no כרת, yet males and females are treated the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let ממזר prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces עריות with a different proof, ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר marrying into the nation does not carry כרת, so the objection of step 22 does not apply. Yet a female ממזרת is forbidden just like a male. So a lighter ban can also forbid women.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the nation

phrases.english: Let a ממזר prove it.
phrases.notes: A ממזר has no כרת, yet the ban covers males and females alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new one that avoids the כרת objection.
steps.raayaObject: That a ban can include females even without being as strict as עריות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of ממזר, which has no כרת yet treats males and females alike

steps.title: ממזר is stricter because it lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the ממזר proof, since a ממזר can never enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare to ממזר? A ממזר is never fit to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ממזר proof with a different strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממזר ban lasts forever, while the מצרי ban ends after three generations. Maybe ממזר women are forbidden because that ban never ends. So ממזר also may not be a fair comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: To enter the congregation, meaning to marry a born Jew
Forever, for all generations

phrases.english: How can you compare to a ממזר,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: since he is never fit to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמַמְזֵר, שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל לְעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ממזר proof of step 23.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ממזר ban is permanent, unlike the three-generation ban of מצרי.

steps.title: Back to forbidden relations, and the argument goes in a circle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with עריות again, which are limited to three generations. The argument has come back to where it started.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let עריות prove it, since they reach only three generations. And the argument has gone back to the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ממזר objection by pointing back to עריות. It notes that the debate has now come full circle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source has its own strictness: עריות have כרת and ממזר lasts forever. But neither strictness is in both, and both still forbid women just like men. So together they seem to show that women are included even in a limited ban. Step 26 spells this out, and step 27 then finds a weakness in it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the argument has returned to the start, going back and forth
The common feature shared by two sources, which proves the rule

steps.whatToRemember: עריות and ממזר together seem to refute רבי שמעון, as step 26 lays out. Step 27 rejects this pair, and the רבנן's real source turns out to be חלל (step 28).
steps.confusionAlert: 'Back to the start' does not mean the proof failed. When two sources knock each other's objections down like this, together they can prove the point, as step 26 lays out. Here, though, step 27 will find a strict feature the two share.

phrases.english: Let forbidden relations prove it,
phrases.notes: עריות are not forever, only three generations, so the 'forever' objection does not apply to them.

phrases.english: and the argument has returned to the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ממזר objection by returning to עריות, closing the cycle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עריות and ממזר answer each other's objections, which leads to the הצד השוה of step 26. That proof is rejected in step 27.

steps.title: Combining the two cases to prove the women are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Each proof alone failed, so the גמרא joins עריות and ממזר. What they share is that both males and females are forbidden, so מצרי and מצרית should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they share is that they are forbidden, both males and females. So I will also bring in a male and female Egyptian, that both are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a new proof by putting the two rejected cases, עריות and ממזר, together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עריות was rejected because it has כרת, and ממזר was rejected because it is forbidden forever. Each has its own weak spot, but neither weak spot appears in both. The one thing they share is that the rule covers males and females equally, so the גמרא applies that to מצרי.

keyTerms.meaning: This case is not like that case; each one has its own special feature
The shared feature: a proof built from what two cases have in common
A male Egyptian convert and a female Egyptian convert
Males and females

steps.confusionAlert: A הצד השוה does not depend on either case alone. It uses only what both cases share, so each case's weak spot no longer matters, unless the two cases share some other strict feature.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה, וְלֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה.
phrases.english: The aspect of this is not like the aspect of that, and the aspect of that is not like the aspect of this.
phrases.notes: 'This' is עריות and 'that' is ממזר, the two proofs that were just rejected.

phrases.english: The feature they share is that they are forbidden,
both males and females alike.
So I too will bring a male Egyptian and a female Egyptian,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ אֲסוּרִין, אֶחָד זְכָרִים וְאֶחָד נְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.english: that they should be forbidden, both males and females.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה, וְלֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the separate proofs from עריות and ממזר were each rejected, the גמרא combines them into one הצד השוה proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the prohibition of a מצרי applies to females as well as males
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature of עריות and ממזר, where both males and females are forbidden

steps.title: The shared proof fails because both cases involve כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the הצד השוה. Both עריות and ממזר have some connection to כרת, which מצרי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about the feature they share? They both have a side of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the combined proof by finding one more strict feature that both cases share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה only works if the two cases share nothing stricter than the case we want to learn. Here both have a 'side of כרת': עריות themselves carry כרת, and a ממזר comes from a forbidden union that carries כרת. מצרי has no כרת at all, so maybe its rule applies only to males.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?': the standard way to point out a difference that breaks a comparison
Since; because (introduces the strict feature)
A side or element of כרת connected to the case

phrases.english: What about the feature they share?
Since they both have a side of כרת.
phrases.notes: עריות carry כרת directly, and a ממזר is born from a union that carries כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן צַד כָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הצד השוה proof of step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole combined proof from עריות and ממזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both source cases share a link to כרת, which מצרי lacks

steps.title: The רבנן learn their point from חלל
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן base their case on חלל, the child of a union that only breaks a positive מצוה‎ (עשה). They follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן learn it from a חלל, from people who broke a positive מצוה, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the real source of the רבנן: חלל, a case with no כרת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלל from a union that only breaks a positive מצוה has no כרת, so the objection from step 27 does not apply. Yet males and females alike become חללים. That this child is a חלל is the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so the רבנן's proof depends on following him.

keyTerms.meaning: A child of a forbidden priestly union, who is unfit for כהונה
Those who break a positive commandment (an עשה), not a 'do not' commandment
The תנא who holds that a child born from a union that breaks an עשה is a חלל

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key point: the רבנן's proof only works if you accept רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and that is exactly where רבי שמעון will disagree.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis learn it from a חלל of those who violate a positive mitzva,
phrases.notes: For example, a כהן גדול who marries a woman who is not a virgin. There is no כרת, only a positive מצוה.

phrases.english: and in accordance with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עריות/ממזר proofs fail, the גמרא names the source the רבנן actually rely on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן's refutation comes from חלל of חייבי עשה, which has no כרת yet applies to both sexes, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: What did רבי שמעון mean by 'Not so'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון meant when he answered the רבנן with 'לא כי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'Not so' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי שמעון's short reply. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן had said that if רבי שמעון's view is a received הלכה they would accept it, but if it is a logical argument, it can be refuted. רבי שמעון answered 'לא כי, הלכה אני אומר.' The גמרא wants to know what 'לא כי' is rejecting.

keyTerms.meaning: And what (does it mean)?
'Not so': רבי שמעון's reply to the רבנן

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'Not so'?
phrases.notes: These are רבי שמעון's words in the משנה, said in reply to the רבנן's challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the רבנן's source (חלל, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב) is known, the גמרא asks how רבי שמעון's reply fits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly רבי שמעון was denying with the words 'לא כי'

steps.title: רבי שמעון's two-level answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says: I don't follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so your proof does not bind me. And even by your view, I am telling you a הלכה I received.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he told them: For me, I do not hold like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. For you, who do hold like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, I am stating a received הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'לא כי' has two layers: rejecting the רבנן's source, and then falling back on a received הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the רבנן's proof from חלל rests on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, whom רבי שמעון does not follow, so it fails for him. Second, even if you accept רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי שמעון is not arguing from logic at all. He is passing on a הלכה he received, and a logical refutation cannot overturn that.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said to them (introduces the explanation)
According to me; in my own view
According to you; in your view
I am stating a received הלכה, not a logical argument

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון permits the מצרית for two reasons. He rejects the רבנן's source, which depends on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. And even without that, his ruling is a received הלכה, which no refutation from logic can overturn.

phrases.english: This is what he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, לָא סְבִירָא לִי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב.
phrases.english: In my own view, I do not hold like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידְכוּ, דִּסְבִירָא לְכוּ כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב —
phrases.english: In your view, since you do hold like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב,
I am stating a received הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ: לְדִידִי, לָא סְבִירָא לִי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29 by explaining the two layers of 'לא כי'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא כי' means: I reject your source because I don't follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and even by your view I am stating a received הלכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's permission of the מצרית rests on a received הלכה, so the רבנן's logical refutation from חלל cannot override it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון adds a verse to his received tradition
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי שמעון said he was stating a received הלכה, and that a פסוק also supports him: 'sons,' not daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון said to them, 'I am telling you a הלכה I received. Also, a פסוק supports me: it says "sons," not daughters.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי שמעון also had a פסוק on his side, not only a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רבי שמעון answered the רבנן by saying he had a received הלכה. Here he adds a second support: the פסוק about the third generation speaks of 'sons.' So the ban on marrying into the קהל applies only to males, and a מצרית is permitted right away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
A law received by tradition
A verse supports me
Sons and not daughters

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon said to them:
I am stating a received halakha,
and furthermore, a verse supports me:
"Sons" — and not daughters.
phrases.notes: דברים 23:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a scriptural support to the received הלכה that רבי שמעון mentioned in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's position that only male מצרים are restricted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'בָּנִים' in the פסוק about the third generation

steps.title: A ברייתא records רבי שמעון's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the word 'sons' excludes daughters, and that this is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Sons' and not daughters. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. This line states רבי שמעון's view and prepares for רבי יהודה to disagree in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling this 'the words of רבי שמעון' tells us it is one side of a מחלוקת, not an agreed rule. The disagreement comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (a ברייתא)
The words of רבי שמעון, his view in a dispute

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Sons" and not daughters,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון's verse-reading is challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the restriction on מצרים applies only to sons.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the verse depends on birth, so daughters are included
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה points to the words 'who are born to them.' The פסוק ties the rule to birth, which includes girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: Look, the פסוק says 'Sons who are born to them in the third generation.' The פסוק made the rule depend on birth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי שמעון by reading the same פסוק a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון focused on the word 'sons.' רבי יהודה focuses on 'who are born to them.' Since daughters are born just like sons, the rule covers both. So a מצרית is also restricted until the third generation.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are born to them
The third generation
Made them depend on birth

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides quote the same פסוק. רבי שמעון reads the word 'sons.' רבי יהודה reads 'born to them.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Look, it says:
"Sons who are born to them
in the third generation,"
the verse made them depend on birth.
phrases.notes: Girls are born just like boys, so daughters are included too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes רבי שמעון's reading of 'בָּנִים' with a reading based on 'יִוָּלְדוּ.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי שמעון's claim that the פסוק excludes daughters
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'sons' is not exclusive, because the פסוק links the rule to birth, which applies to females too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה had to say this
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that without his 'depends on birth' reading, רבי יהודה would have been stuck in the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If רבי יהודה had not said 'the פסוק made them depend on birth,' he would not have found his hands and feet in the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן comments that רבי יהודה's reading was necessary for him. Without it, his other views would not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument about the פסוק. רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה's position must include daughters, or he would contradict another view of his own. The גמרא explains how in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for
He would be stuck, unable to defend himself
The study hall

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
If Rabbi Yehuda had not said
the verse made them depend on birth —
he would not have found his hands and feet
phrases.notes: A saying that means he'd be stuck, with no way to defend his position.

phrases.english: in the study hall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on רבי יהודה's reading from step 33 and calls it necessary for his overall system.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה needed to include daughters in the restriction to avoid contradicting himself.

steps.title: Beginning the explanation: converts count as a קהל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining רבי יוחנן's statement. It recalls that, according to רבי יהודה, a group of converts is called a קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said: a group of converts is called a קהל,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain why רבי יהודה would be stuck otherwise. This line lays down the first piece of background; the explanation continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that converts count as a 'קהל ה'.' That matters for whom a first- or second-generation מצרי or מצרית may marry. This background is what would clash with excluding daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: Since the Master said
A congregation of converts
Is called a קהל, the congregation of ה'

phrases.english: Since the Master said:
a congregation of converts is called a congregation,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה's view, and the sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: קְהַל גֵּרִים אִיקְּרִי קָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining why רבי יוחנן said רבי יהודה would be stuck without his reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יהודה would contradict himself without the 'depends on birth' reading (implied question)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It begins from רבי יהודה's view that a group of converts is called a קהל; the rest continues past this point.
